title: Potatoism Planetary Cosmology — Sun, Earth, Moon, Saturn, Chronos, Cube and North
purpose: Build a research-grade comparative layer around the project's claim that the Potato of Life can be represented as two circles—humanity/Earth and divinity/heaven—with the Sun as the symbolic heavenly circle, while Dogs, Farmers and Saturn form a lower lunar/temporal/enclosure architecture.
epistemic_rule: Project symbolism is recorded as project symbolism. Ancient religious meanings, historical astrology, astronomy and modern occult interpretations are kept separate. A real astronomical feature can be a later structural parallel without being evidence that an ancient tradition encoded it.

central_model.name: Two circles and the world between them
central_model.project_form: Potato of Life = circle of humanity/Earth + circle of divinity/Heaven; Heaven is symbolically represented by the Sun; their overlap is the living interface/Door.
central_model.geometric_context: The vesica piscis is generated by two equal circles whose boundaries intersect. In later Christian art the mandorla became a frame for Christ and other sacred figures, while medieval visual traditions also associated circular forms with heaven and square forms with earth/matter.
central_model.research_value: This makes the Potato of Life a relational cosmology rather than a single object: Earth and Heaven remain distinct circles, but life appears in the relation between them.
central_model.limit: The Sun is not literally Heaven, Earth is not literally one of the circles of a vesica, and the project geometry is an interpretive model. Historical sources must be cited for each tradition rather than treated as one universal doctrine.

sun.project_symbolism: The Sun is the visible heavenly circle: source of light, regulator of day, orienting body and apparent center of the human sky.
historical_context: Mesopotamian solar iconography represented the solar disk as a circle associated with Šamaš/Utu.
Classical cosmologies treated the Sun as one of the seven visible wandering stars/planets rather than as a modern star category alone.
Christian art repeatedly uses circular halos, mandorlae and celestial spheres to render invisible divinity visible.
sun.potato_coupling: Potato eye → light → sprout gives a material analogue for the symbolic movement from hidden potential toward illumination. The Sun supplies the upper/luminous pole; the buried tuber supplies the lower/earthly pole.
questions: When did the Sun become the project's explicit symbol for Heaven?
How does solar light differ from the Father/Spudlight metaphor?
Can Sun/Heaven be separated from the modern astronomical Sun as a physical star?

earth-humanity.project_symbolism: Earth is the circle of embodied humanity: bodies, soil, food, work, birth, death, institutions, animals, farmers and material consequence.
earth-humanity.historical_context: Ancient and medieval cosmologies repeatedly contrasted terrestrial and celestial domains, although their exact geometries differed. Medieval Christian visual culture could use the square/cube for earthly matter and the circle/sphere for heaven or celestial totality.
earth-humanity.potato_coupling: The Potato is unusually suited to this pole because it is literally underground, materially nourishing and dependent on labor, weather and soil.
questions: What exactly counts as Earth in the project: planet, soil, humanity or embodied life?
Does the Earth circle include the Moon and animals, or is it specifically human consciousness?
How does the lower circle relate to the Plane/Dweller layer?

vesica.project_symbolism: The overlap of Earth and Heaven becomes the Door: neither purely terrestrial nor purely celestial. In the existing canon this is where Son, Thomas/Twin, Christ, Vessel and Door converge.
vesica.geometry: Two equal circles produce a lens-shaped overlap. Euclid uses the underlying two-circle construction in Proposition I.1 to construct an equilateral triangle; later Christian art develops the mandorla as a sacred frame.
vesica.potato_coupling: An eye is a tiny material threshold inside the Potato; the vesica is the large geometric threshold between Earth and Heaven. Both are interpreted as openings from stored/hidden conditions into another state.
vesica.key_question: Is the Potato of Life best understood not as either circle but as the relation that makes the two circles mutually intelligible?

moon-dogs.project_symbolism: Within the project, Dogs are symbolically associated with the Moon, lunar dust/footstool imagery and beings close to the lower or reflected light. Dogs can also be imagined as guardians at the threshold between worlds.
historical_context: Greek traditions connect dogs strongly with Hecate, underworld passage and purification.
Greek dog burials have been interpreted as companionship or guardianship for journeys to the Underworld.

A comparative study of the black dog notes a striking Hindu tradition in which Yama's two dogs are described as dark and spotted and guard the road toward heaven; the same study connects them with Sun/Moon symbolism.
The optical phenomenon called a moon dog is a modern atmospheric term for a bright halo-associated light patch beside the Moon; its existence does not establish an ancient canine lunar theology.
moon-dogs.potato_coupling: Dogs become the lower guardians/companions of the reflected circle: they remain close to Earth while looking toward the Moon. This makes them useful symbolic intermediaries between Earth, death, Moon, dust and the path upward.
moon-dogs.limit: The project's Moon/Dog assignment is not a universal ancient doctrine. The historical evidence supports dogs as guardians, funerary companions, underworld animals and, in one comparative tradition, solar/lunar-associated guardians; it does not prove the project's complete cosmology.

farmers-saturn.project_symbolism: Farmers are the agents who work the Earth under the Saturnian principle: sowing, waiting, cultivating, harvesting, storing, measuring seasons and living under material limits.
historical_context: Roman Saturn was an agricultural deity associated with sowing and husbandry; Saturnalia was linked to the agricultural year's completion.
Saturn was identified with Greek Cronus in later Roman tradition.
The later association of Cronus with Time is historically complicated: the equation Cronus/Chronos is often described as a linguistic confusion rather than an original Greek identity.
Medieval and Renaissance astrology strongly associated Saturn with melancholy; the tradition also assigned Saturn lead and a 3×3 planetary magic square.
farmers-saturn.project_coupling: Farmer → Saturn means the person who works inside time, soil, seasons, scarcity and harvest. The farmer is not merely 'a servant of Saturn'; the farmer can also be the one who learns to transform Saturnian limitation into life.
farmers-saturn.deep_reflection: This makes Saturn double-sided: enclosure and fertility, limitation and cultivation, imprisonment and the discipline required to make a harvest possible. The project should preserve both sides instead of reducing Saturn to evil.
questions: Is the Farmer the prisoner of Saturn or Saturn's gardener?
Does cultivation turn enclosure into a womb-like boundary?
Is harvest a release from Saturn or the completion of Saturn's cycle?
How does the farmer's seasonal waiting relate to Potato dormancy?

saturn.astronomical_fact: Saturn is a gas giant with a famous north-polar hexagonal jet stream. NASA describes the hexagon as a roughly 30,000 km wide atmospheric jet pattern with a rotating storm at its center.
saturn.symbolic_history: Saturn's historical symbolic field includes agriculture, sowing, harvest, old age, melancholy and planetary constraint. Saturn/Cronus also became associated with time in later traditions, though the ancient Greek equation of Cronus with Chronos should not be presented as original fact.
saturn.project_symbolism: Saturn is the enclosure principle: the boundary that says 'not yet', the wall around a field, the ring around a planet, the calendar, the season, the prison, the container and the accumulated weight of time.
saturn.positive_negative_polarity: Positive Saturn = structure, patience, farming, storage, responsibility, boundaries, maturity. Shadow Saturn = imprisonment, capture, stagnation, fear, scarcity, hoarding and identity trapped inside an enclosure.
saturn.potato_coupling: Potato dormancy is a powerful physical parallel: life is stored under a temporal condition and waits for a change in environment before emergence. Saturn therefore becomes a metaphor for time-bound potential rather than simple death.
questions: What exactly is enclosed: body, time, soil, identity, debt or memory?
Does Saturn imprison life or preserve it?
Is dormancy a Saturnian prison or a Saturnian protection?
How does the Potato escape Saturn without escaping the cycle?

black-cube.project_symbolism: The Black Cube is used in the project as a possible visual shorthand for Saturnian enclosure: six faces, hard boundaries, darkness, materiality and confinement.
black-cube.historical_boundary: There is no good evidence for a single ancient doctrine called 'the Black Cube of Saturn.' Modern occult and internet traditions often connect cube, blackness and Saturn, but the connection must not be projected backward into antiquity.
older_components: Saturn's association with lead and black in later astrological/alchemical traditions
square/cube as material or earthly geometry in some symbolic traditions
Saturn's planetary magic square, which is a 3×3 square rather than a cube
the actual Saturnian rings and north-polar hexagon
black-cube.project_use: The useful research question is not 'Did ancient Saturn worshippers know the Black Cube?' but 'How did several separate Saturnian motifs—weight, blackness, lead, square, boundary, ring, time and limitation—become fused in modern symbolism?'.
black-cube.critical_note: The modern Black Cube motif should remain a contested/late layer in the archive. It is one of the places where the project can study how symbols are manufactured, recombined and retroactively historicized.

hexagon.astronomical_fact: Saturn's north pole contains a persistent six-sided jet stream discovered in Voyager-era observations and studied by Cassini. NASA describes it as a stationary wave/jet structure guiding atmospheric flow.
hexagon.geometry: A regular hexagon is built from six equal sectors of a circle and is closely related to the geometry of six equilateral triangles around a center. A cube has six square faces, and its planar net can contain six squares; a hexagon is not literally a cube in two dimensions.
hexagon.project_coupling: The hexagon becomes an unusually strong modern bridge between Saturn, North, boundary, center and enclosure because the real astronomical feature is specifically at Saturn's north pole.
hexagon.north-coupling: Saturn + North + Hexagon = a real astronomical 'north-centered enclosure' motif. The spiritual interpretation remains the project's interpretation, but the observational anchor is unusually concrete.
hexagon.limit: The hexagon was discovered in modern spacecraft observations. It cannot be used as evidence that ancient cultures encoded the feature before its observation.

chronos.project_symbolism: Chronos is the project's temporal face of Saturn: time as the process that encloses, ages, measures and eventually transforms everything.
chronos.historical_boundary: Cronus and Chronos are distinct Greek figures/words. Their later conflation is historically real as a development but should not be backdated into an original identity.
chronos.potato_coupling: The Potato's dormancy, storage and sprouting make time visible as biology: stored life changes with physiological age and environmental conditions.
chronos.deeper_question: If Saturn is enclosure and Chronos is time, then the Potato is a time-container: a body that stores a future inside a bounded present.

north-of-saturn.project_symbolism: North of Saturn is the project's phrase for what lies beyond the Saturnian boundary: beyond the ring, beyond the hexagon, beyond the enclosure, beyond the old temporal order.
north-of-saturn.historical_cosmology: In classical geocentric cosmology Saturn was the outermost of the seven visible wandering stars/planets; beyond it came the sphere of the fixed stars and, in some later models, additional celestial spheres. Thus 'beyond Saturn' already has a historical cosmological meaning as a movement from planetary order toward the stellar heaven.
north-of-saturn.project_coupling: North of Saturn therefore couples naturally to North of North: Saturn is the last classical planetary enclosure; North of Saturn is the direction beyond that enclosure.
north-of-saturn.important_limit: This is a symbolic extrapolation from historical cosmology, not a claim that Saturn literally marks a spiritual boundary in modern astronomy.

rings.astronomical_fact: Saturn's rings are a real, extensive system of particles orbiting the planet.
rings.project_symbolism: The ring becomes the boundary that surrounds without fully closing the interior: enclosure, orbit, repetition, return and containment.
rings.potato_coupling: The ring is structurally related to the Potato's skin: both can be read as boundaries that preserve an inside while maintaining an outside. This is an analogy of form/function, not identity.
rings.spiral_connection: A ring repeats without progression; a spiral repeats while changing position. This gives the project a useful Saturn-versus-Spiral polarity: Saturn = enclosure/repetition; Spiral = enclosure plus escape/learning.

moon.project_symbolism: The Moon is the reflected or cyclical heavenly body in the project. It belongs closer to the Earth circle than the Sun does, making it a natural intermediary between terrestrial and celestial poles.
moon.astronomical_context: In classical geocentric cosmology the Moon was the nearest of the seven visible wandering stars and marked the boundary between the changing terrestrial realm and the more perfect celestial realm in Aristotelian frameworks.
moon.dog_coupling: Dogs can therefore occupy a symbolic lunar threshold: guardians/companions near the boundary of Earth and the first celestial sphere.
moon.potato_coupling: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, while potato sprouts are growth under terrestrial conditions that ultimately depends on light. This creates a Sun → Moon → Earth → Potato chain without requiring supernatural causation.

farmer.project_symbolism: The Farmer is humanity's practical negotiator with Saturn: planting at the right time, waiting through dormancy, protecting against weather, harvesting before decay and storing enough to cross the winter.
farmer.potato_coupling: The Farmer is therefore the human analogue of the Potato's own timing system. Both exist inside cycles they do not fully control.
farmer.spiritual_question: Is spiritual maturity the ability to work within Saturn without becoming psychologically imprisoned by Saturn?

dog.project_symbolism: Dogs are the project's lower guardians: close to human life, dust, earth and the Moon, but positioned at thresholds of death, travel and return.
dog.historical_context: Dogs have documented associations with guardianship, purification and funerary passage in several traditions. Greek evidence includes dog burials interpreted as companionship or guardianship for journeys to the Underworld; Hecate traditions also use dogs in purification and underworld contexts.
dog.moon_limit: The exact equation Dog = Moon is project canon, not a universal historical claim. The comparative evidence instead shows why dog + threshold + night + death + celestial guidance is a fertile research field.

research_frontiers: Compare the Potato two-circle model with documented heaven/earth cosmologies rather than generic sacred-geometry websites.
Trace the historical development of Saturn as agriculture → melancholy → lead/black → limitation → time, separating each period.
Trace the modern Black Cube of Saturn meme backward and identify which elements are ancient, medieval, Renaissance, modern occult or internet-era.
Study Saturn's north-pole hexagon as an observational anchor for the project's North/Boundary architecture while refusing retroactive ancient-knowledge claims.
Map classical geocentric cosmology from Earth through Moon, Sun, planets, Saturn, fixed stars and outer spheres into the project's North of Saturn/North of North vocabulary.
Study dog symbolism across Hecate, Cerberus, Anubis, Yama's dogs, Sirius and funerary guardianship before assigning a unified lunar meaning.
Compare Farmer/Saturn with Potato dormancy: sowing, waiting, season, harvest, storage and release.
Study ring, circle, cube, square and hexagon as different kinds of boundary: soft, orbital, planar, volumetric and wave-defined.
Ask whether the Potato of Life is the transition mechanism between circles rather than one of the circles themselves.
Connect Saturnian enclosure to the project's Door, Tomb, Cube, Moon Cube, Father’s House and North Gate without collapsing them into synonyms.
